Emma (Product): Quick q — when we save a per-route saved query that pins a model and sets routing hints, should the Console's cost/latency preview default to the pinned model? users keep getting previews that don't match saved behavior.

Raj (Eng): I lean yes. Preview should reflect what the route will actually use. Otherwise you save -> deploy -> surprise. But backend needs an explicit model_id in the saved query proto (we only have a model_hint today).

Maria (Console UX): +1. From a UX POV we also need an explicit toggle: 'Preview as saved config' vs 'Preview as live route'. Otherwise people will be confused. The default should be 'saved config' when viewing a savedquery.

Noah (Backend): Note: current GET /savedqueries returns filter_json + model_hint string. We don't run routing policy when returning savedqueries. To preview accurately we either simulate routing client-side (risky) or call the routing service server-side. Prefer server-side so we use the real placement/capacity logic.

Liz (Telemetry): Important — mark preview traffic in telemetry so it doesn't pollute real usage metrics. Use preview_flag + preview_model_id. Also we should rate-limit preview endpoint to avoid cost explosion.

Emma (Product): Could we do a cheap client-side approximation for the first pass? Might unblock UI experiments.

Raj (Eng): Client-side won't capture fallback tiers or regional routing. You'll get optimistic cost numbers. If we accept that tradeoff we must label them clearly. Long-term: new POST /savedqueries/preview that calls routing-service.apply and returns deterministic routing decision.

Maria (Console UX): UX details: show a small badge "Preview mode: as saved config" and show why model chosen (pinned vs fallback) + a short warning if preview hits a lower-tier variant. Also show token breakdown and cost delta. Example microcopy: "Estimate based on model v2-small; actual may differ if capacity changes."

ops-bot: routing-service v2 scheduled for deploy Tue 03:00 UTC (rollout: canary -> 50% -> global).

Noah (Backend): API sketch (draft):
```
POST /savedqueries/preview
body: { saved_query_id, route_id, preview_mode: "pinned_model" | "route_default" | "cost_opt" }
resp: { model_used, deterministic_model_id, estimated_tokens, latency_p95_ms, cost_estimate_cents, reason_flags: ["fallback","quantized","pin-mismatch"] }
```
We should also include a cached response key so clients can reuse short-lived previews.

Raj (Eng): Add field deterministic_model_id when a route pins an exact version (helps console deep-links + telemetry joins). Also include route_policy_version so we can trace preview mismatches after rollouts.

Maria (Console UX): For rollout UX: can we persist a per-user preview preference? e.g., last used preview_mode stored in user settings so experiments don't constantly flip people between modes. Small cookie or account pref.

Liz (Telemetry): Telemetry keys: preview=true/false, preview_mode, preview_model_id, preview_policy_version, preview_sample_id. Emit a trace/span when preview endpoint calls routing-service so we can debug mismatches.

Emma (Product): Action items: Noah spec + auth for endpoint; Raj hook routing apply & add route_policy_version; Maria mock UI + copy; Liz add telemetry schema; ops watch deploy. I'll follow up in a short RFC. Thanks all :heart:

Noah (Backend): I can have a first-pass spec by EOD tomorrow. Will add conservative rate-limits (per-user and global) and memoization TTL 60s.

Raj (Eng): I'll prototype server-side call and return shape in the backend sandbox.

Maria (Console UX): I'll post mock screenshots to #design later today and include copy for the preview badge.

Liz (Telemetry): I'll add the keys to the telemetry contract and a couple test dashboards to catch preview leakage into billing.

Emma (Product): Great — thanks team. Ping me once specs are up so I can write the RFC. :smile:
